brief: Early morning in the temple library: Śuka the parrot at an open window with the sunrise behind him, beak wide open mid-squawk, wings half spread; Dādī at the reading desk lowering her round spectacles with one eyebrow raised, amused; Dhūmaka giggling as a little puff of smoke beside the glowing leaf.

Evening in the temple library. On the low reading desk the half-burnt palm leaf glows gold. Smoke from a brass oil lamp curls upward and gathers into Dhūmaka, a small round smoke-grey ghost with big kind eyes, pointing at the leaf. You (seen from behind) and Dādī lean in; Śuka on your shoulder puffs his feathers in surprise.

brief: The glowing palm leaf: beneath the bright first line, a second line of small Devanagari words is beginning to glow, the little vowel marks above and below the letters catching the light first. The words are small and soft-focus, with no legible text. Dhūmaka trembles, pointing at one word; Dādī leans in, spectacles on.

Deep forest under a great banyan tree: the poet Guṇāḍhya writes on palm leaves with a reed pen dipped in a small dark-red pot (no wound shown). Spirits of soft blue light and forest animals gather at a distance, listening. Calm, reverent, golden evening light.

A hilltop at dusk: Guṇāḍhya reads aloud from a palm leaf beside a small fire, a tear on his cheek; deer, boars, buffaloes and birds sit in a quiet circle listening; two pupils watch sadly; one leaf curls into the flames.

Present day, evening, in the temple library: you (seen from behind) and Dādī at the low reading desk; a half-burnt palm leaf has begun to glow faintly gold; Śuka the parrot on your shoulder; brass lamps, shelves of palm-leaf bundles.
